Asks we need to finalize pricing options

   - Target steady-state (12 months): 18–30M tokens/mo
2) Budget range you can commit to for the Pilot & Prod phases (monthly): pls give low/target/high.
3) Target $/1M tokens you want us to model for both hosted and dedicated (if you prefer a reserved capacity discount).
4) Any strict latency or regional constraints (we noted EU data residency for some clients).

What we'll deliver after you confirm

- Competitive benchmark vs OpenAI / Anthropic / common open-hosts at the requested target points.

I've attached a blank token-plan worksheet (Finlytics_MAAP_1M_token_plan.xlsx) — fill the green cells or reply with numbers and we'll run the unit-econ model.

Ben / Sofia — quick internal notes and a suggested benchmarking slice for the MAAP. I'll put formal numbers in the shared worksheet but wanted to capture rationale here.

Suggested target tiers to present (net $/1M tokens after standard discounts):
- Tier A (reserved, 12m commit): $9 / 1M (for >20M/mo steady-state) — requires reservation and some capacity commitment; best unit cost but longer term.
- Tier B (reserved, 3–6m commit): $18 / 1M (for 8–20M/mo) — middle ground, good for pilots that plan to scale.
- Tier C (hosted, pay-as-you-go): $35 / 1M — includes dynamic routing, global endpoints, and full observability; no commit.

Competitor benchmark (high level, public + market estimate):
- OpenAI (GPT-4-class conversational workloads): roughly $80–$140 / 1M tokens (depends on model variant and prompt/response length).
- Anthropic (Claude-family): roughly $60–$110 / 1M tokens for similar classes.
- Open-model hosting providers (managed Llama/GGML-style stacks): commonly $8–$30 / 1M depending on quantization and whether dedicated infra is used.

Notes on tradeoffs:
- Lower $/1M (open-hosts / dedicated) often implies less consistent tail-latency and more ops coordination (model variant, quantization choices).
- Hosted pay-as-you-go preserves developer velocity and simplifies fallbacks, but unit cost is higher; caching/prefix reuse can shave effective per-token cost for chat-heavy flows.
- For EU data residency we'll propose routing Pilot EU traffic to Dedicated EU-capacity (adds ~10–15% premium in the reserved pricing due to regional infra costs).

I'll add these rows to the MAAP workbook and a short slide summarizing quality vs cost tradeoffs. Also linking the deal in HubSpot for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567890
